entries.name: Artificial Analysis
entries.why: Probably the strongest single public model-comparison surface today because it independently runs models and combines intelligence with price, latency and throughput. Its current Intelligence Index uses ten evaluations spanning agents, coding, science and general capability.

verification.note: Claims consistent: Intelligence Index v4.3.2 aggregates 10 evaluations (e.g. GDPval-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, HLE). Jan 2024 launch per founders' Latent Space interview, not an AA page.

entries.name: Epoch AI Capabilities & Benchmarking / ECI
entries.why: Exceptionally strong research-grade longitudinal capability tracking. It currently tracks hundreds of models and dozens of benchmarks and exposes methodology/data rather than only a leaderboard.

verification.note: Official names: AI Benchmarking Hub (27 Nov 2024) and Epoch Capabilities Index (Oct 2025). Hub now lists 401 models, 86 benchmarks, consistent with claims. ECI paper co-authored with Google DeepMind.

entries.name: Arena.ai / LM Arena
entries.why: Best large-scale real-user preference signal. It measures utility that static QA benchmarks miss through anonymous pairwise human judgments. LMArena rebranded to Arena in January 2026.

verification.note: Rebrand to Arena (arena.ai) announced 28 Jan 2026, consistent. Former name was 'LMArena' (one word), originally Chatbot Arena launched by LMSYS on 3 May 2023.

entries.name: METR
entries.why: Critical for long-horizon autonomous capability, human-calibrated task horizons and AI-R&D evaluation. METR itself warns that time-horizon estimates have large uncertainty and are approaching saturation—exactly the methodological transparency a serious evaluation program should provide.

verification.note: Claims consistent. Spun out of ARC Evals as METR Dec 2023; time-horizon paper Mar 2025; Time Horizon 1.1 page (metr.org/time-horizons) says >16h measurements unreliable.

entries.name: Mercor Research / APEX
entries.why: One of the strongest directions in 2026: economically valuable real work rather than academic QA. APEX now spans professional services, long-horizon agents, accounting and software engineering.

verification.note: APEX = AI Productivity Index. Family confirmed: APEX-v1 (four professions), APEX-Agents, APEX-SWE, APEX-Accounting. APEX-v1 leaderboard uses held-out cases; only examples open-sourced.

entries.name: Scale SEAL Leaderboards
entries.why: Important because test data are private, domain experts grade outputs, and contamination/gaming resistance is explicitly part of the design.

verification.note: List link is the 29 May 2024 SEAL launch post. scale.com/leaderboard now 308-redirects to labs.scale.com, branded Scale Labs with no 'SEAL'; now mixes private and open datasets.

entries.name: SWE-bench
entries.why: Still one of the canonical real-repository agent/coding measures. Actual GitHub issue resolution is significantly more informative than function-generation benchmarks.

verification.note: Claims consistent. Family includes Full, Lite, Verified (Aug 2024), Multimodal (v2 fully open-sourced Sep 2026), Multilingual and bash-only leaderboards.

entries.name: ARC Prize / ARC-AGI
entries.why: High-value signal for abstraction/generalization rather than memorized knowledge. Maintains explicit verification policies and cost/task reporting.

verification.note: Claims consistent: leaderboard covers ARC-AGI-1/2/3 with cost per task; verified testing policy uses Semi-Private set, $10k/run cap. ARC-AGI-2/3 repos under github.com/arcprize.

entries.name: Terminal-Bench + Harbor
entries.why: One of the most consequential 2026 agent evaluations: real terminal environments, difficult evolving tasks, executable verification and standardized Harbor execution.

verification.note: Claims consistent. Launched 19 May 2025; TB 2.0 + Harbor Nov 2025; TB 3.0 Jul 2026; TB 4.0 (28 Aug 2026) current. Harbor repo: github.com/harbor-framework/harbor.

entries.name: Inspect AI — UK AISI
entries.why: The strongest open-source general frontier-evaluation framework in my ordering: datasets, agents, tools, scorers, sandboxes, MCP, external agents and 200+ ready-to-run evaluations.

verification.note: Claims consistent: site cites 'over 200 pre-built evaluations', MCP tools, sandboxes, external agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI). Released May 2024 by then-AI Safety Institute.

entries.name: LiveBench
entries.why: Designed explicitly against contamination, with new questions introduced over time rather than freezing a static benchmark forever.

verification.note: Latest changelog release is 2026-01-08; nothing newer found despite 'monthly' design. README says newest releases are not fully public on Hugging Face.

entries.name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard — BFCL
entries.why: Tool calling has become core agent infrastructure. BFCL V4 moves beyond trivial function selection toward multi-turn and agentic evaluation.

verification.note: Claims consistent: V1 Feb 2024, V2 Aug 2024, V3 multi-turn Sep 2024, V4 agentic (web search, memory) Jul 2025; page last updated 2026-04-12. Paper at ICML 2025.

entries.name: τ³-bench
entries.why: Evaluates policy following, user interaction and tool execution under dynamic environments; materially closer to production agents than static QA. The original τ-bench repository now explicitly points users toward τ³.

verification.note: Claims consistent: original tau-bench repo points to τ³. τ³-bench 1.0.0 released 18 Mar 2026 inside tau2-bench repo (voice, knowledge, task fixes); v1.0.1 Jul 2026.

entries.name: Stanford HELM
entries.why: Strong methodology, standardized scenarios and broad evaluation philosophy. Especially useful where transparency across metrics matters more than a single number.

verification.note: Claims consistent. Paper v1 16 Nov 2022 (TMLR 2023); repo still maintained (last commit Jun 2026).

entries.name: OpenCompass
entries.why: Major open evaluation stack supporting 100+ datasets, proprietary/open models and increasingly multimodal evaluation. Active 2026 development matters here.

verification.note: Claims consistent: repo cites 100+ datasets; active in 2026 (v0.5.4 Aug 2026, commits Sep 2026, VLMEvalKit multimodal integration). Platform paper on arXiv May 2026.

entries.name: OpenAI Evals API / Graders
entries.why: Important for production evaluation pipelines, model graders and application-specific eval sets rather than public leaderboard comparison.

verification.note: Being deprecated: announced 3 Jun 2026; Evals read-only 31 Oct 2026, shutdown 30 Nov 2026; graders also deprecated. OpenAI points to Datasets instead. Evals launched Oct 2024.

entries.name: OpenAI Evals OSS
entries.why: Mature reference architecture for defining model/system evals and private/custom eval datasets.

verification.note: Open-sourced with GPT-4 (Mar 2023, per GPT-4 technical report). Low activity: last commit Apr 2026; README steers users to Dashboard Evals, which shuts down 30 Nov 2026.

entries.name: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness
entries.why: Still foundational infrastructure. It implements 60+ standard benchmarks, numerous backends and underpins major open-model evaluation workflows. It remains actively maintained in 2026.

verification.note: Claims consistent: README says 'over 60 standard academic benchmarks'; active (v0.4.13 Aug 2026, commits Sep 2026). First commit Aug 2020; first PyPI release Sep 2021.

entries.name: FrontierMath
entries.why: Strong because the problems are deliberately unpublished/extremely difficult; newer variants include research-level and open mathematical problems.

verification.note: Claims consistent: Tiers 1–4 (Tier 4 research-level), Open Problems, and FrontierMath Erdős (launched 3 Sep 2026; Lean proofs of open Erdős problems).

entries.name: LiveCodeBench
entries.why: Better contamination profile than static coding datasets because it continuously draws from recently released competitive-programming problems.

verification.note: List link github.com/GOTOIA/livecodebench is a 0-star fork; official is LiveCodeBench/LiveCodeBench. Refresh looks stalled: latest release_v6 (problems to Apr 2025), last commit Jul 2025.

entries.name: Humanity's Last Exam
entries.why: Extremely difficult multi-domain expert knowledge/reasoning; useful while frontier separation remains substantial.

verification.note: Claims consistent. 2,500 questions; published in Nature 2026; variants HLE-Rolling (Oct 2025) and HLE-Diamond (22 Sep 2026).

entries.name: GDPval
entries.why: Real occupational deliverables rather than exam-style QA; covers economically relevant tasks across occupations.

verification.note: Claims consistent: 44 occupations, 9 sectors, 1,320 tasks; 220-task gold subset open, grader at evals.openai.com. openai.com returns 403 to automated fetches; page confirmed via search.

entries.name: APEX-Agents
entries.why: Multi-hour professional tasks across files, communications and productivity applications. Updated to 1.1 in September 2026.

verification.note: Claims consistent: v1.1 announced 8 Sep 2026 (240 tasks, 80 each in banking, consulting, law; anti-hedging judge). v1 paper (Jan 2026) had 480 tasks.

entries.name: APEX-SWE
entries.why: Focuses on economically valuable integration and observability engineering rather than toy coding.

verification.note: Claims consistent: integration + observability tasks, 200 hidden, 50 open dev. List link is the generic APEX methodology page; the dedicated leaderboard is the better link.

entries.name: OSWorld 2.0
entries.why: Long-horizon GUI/computer interaction in real operating-system environments. OSWorld 2.0/2.1 is the current branch in 2026.

verification.note: List link redirects to the OSWorld 1.0 page (osworld-v1.xlang.ai). OSWorld 2.0 (108 tasks) released 26 Jun 2026; v2.1 16 Sep 2026. 'released' is original OSWorld.

entries.name: RE-Bench
entries.why: Measures AI agents against human experts on research-engineering tasks; valuable for autonomous AI-R&D capability.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. The v1 paper covers 7 ML research-engineering environments and 71 eight-hour attempts by human experts.

entries.name: BrowseComp
entries.why: Measures persistent, strategic search for difficult-to-find facts; designed around easy verification but difficult discovery.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source (1,266 questions). The OpenAI page returns 403 to bots but search results confirm it. simple-evals, which holds the reference implementation, stopped updating in July 2025.

entries.name: DeepResearchBench II
entries.why: Long-form web research, information recall, analysis and presentation. Current professional research-agent signal.

verification.note: Official spelling is 'DeepResearch Bench II' (USTC, 132 tasks; Mercor says 130). The list's link is Mercor's third-party page. Not Epoch's 'DeepResearchBench', a separate benchmark by FutureSearch.

entries.name: TheAgentCompany
entries.why: Simulated software-company tasks involving browsing, coding, communication and work applications.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source (175 tasks in a simulated software company). Epoch lists it as 'The Agent Company'.

entries.name: GAIA
entries.why: Multi-step general-agent benchmark with tools/files and private test answers; still actively maintained.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. 466 questions, with answers withheld for 300 test questions. The public-results dataset on Hugging Face was updated recently, so the benchmark is still maintained.

entries.name: SWE-Lancer
entries.why: Real freelance engineering tasks linked to actual monetary value and end-to-end verification.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. The original repo, openai/SWELancer-Benchmark, was archived in July 2025 and merged into openai/preparedness, which now redirects to frontier-evals. Only the Diamond split is public.

entries.name: Aider Polyglot
entries.why: Particularly useful for realistic edit-based coding rather than isolated function generation.

verification.note: The list links to GitHub source markdown; the canonical page is aider.chat. 225 Exercism exercises. Last updated 2025-11-20, with newest scores from Aug 2025, so it is stale for 2026.

entries.name: SciCode
entries.why: Research-derived coding problems across physics, biology, chemistry, mathematics and materials science.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 80 main problems and 338 subproblems across physics, math, materials science, biology and chemistry.

entries.name: AgentDojo
entries.why: Stateful agent benchmark combining legitimate task utility with prompt-injection attack success.
entries.org: ETH Zurich SPY Lab; Invariant Labs

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 97 tasks and 629 security test cases, measuring utility together with prompt-injection attack success.

entries.name: WebArena
entries.why: Interactive web environments and execution-based success.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. webarena.dev is now the WebArena-x hub, which also hosts WebArena-Infinity, VisualWebArena and TheAgentCompany.

entries.name: BrowserGym
entries.why: Useful common environment/harness for browser-agent evaluation.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. It was first introduced in the WorkArena paper (arXiv 2403.07718, Mar 2024); the ecosystem paper followed in Dec 2024. It supports WebArena, VisualWebArena, WorkArena and others.

entries.name: VisualWebArena
entries.why: Adds visual web understanding to browser task execution.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 910 visually grounded tasks across Classifieds, Shopping and Reddit sites (ACL 2024).

entries.name: WorkArena
entries.why: Work-oriented web application tasks; useful for enterprise agent evaluation.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source. It has 33 atomic ServiceNow tasks, and WorkArena++ (arXiv 2407.05291) adds 682 composite tasks. Instances are gated on Hugging Face.

entries.name: τ^τ-bench / Hyper-τ
entries.why: Tests an outer coding agent constructing a functioning customer-service agent, then evaluates it through τ-style interactions.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 53 tasks across 4 domains, scored with held-out simulated users. The best configuration reaches 23.9%, against an 82.2% expert reference. It is pronounced 'hyper-tau-bench'.

entries.name: Remote Labor Index
entries.why: Measures agent ability against remote-work tasks; included in Epoch's current capability benchmark ecosystem.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 240 freelance projects (230 private test, 10 public). It is listed on Epoch's ECI included-benchmarks page.

entries.name: APEX-1
entries.why: High-value banking, consulting, law and medicine deliverables.

verification.note: Launched as 'APEX' (AI Productivity Index v1.0, 200 held-out cases), now APEX-v1-extended (400 held-out). Mercor labels it 'APEX-1'. The four domains match the list.

entries.name: APEX-Accounting
entries.why: Real reconciliation, statements, audit and tax workflows.

verification.note: arXiv and Mercor blog date it Jul 2026; Mercor's methodology page says March 2026. Paper tasks are reconciliation, accruals, posting and reports. The list's 'statements/audit/tax' matches only the methodology page.

entries.name: ACE / AI Consumer Index
entries.why: Evaluates realistic shopping, food, DIY and gaming tasks rather than academic questions.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 400 hidden cases plus an 80-case open dev set. As of 2026-09-25 the ACE leaderboard URL redirects to /apex/, and ACE is no longer listed there.

entries.name: SimpleQA Verified
entries.why: High-quality verified factual knowledge benchmark; useful as a clean factual layer rather than a holistic intelligence metric.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: 1,000 prompts filtered from OpenAI's SimpleQA. The dataset is on Hugging Face (google/simpleqa-verified). Epoch runs it itself.

entries.name: MirrorCode
entries.why: Reimplementation of entire software programs rather than isolated functions; part of Epoch's current frontier suite.

verification.note: Preliminary results came out 2026-04-10; code and paper in Jun 2026. 22 of 25 targets are open, 3 private. The list's link is Epoch's generic registry, not the MirrorCode page.

entries.name: DeepSWE v1.1
entries.why: Stronger emphasis on repository-level software agent performance.

verification.note: This is Datacurve's benchmark: 113 tasks, v1.0 on 2026-05-26 and v1.1 on 2026-06-14. It is not Agentica/Together AI's 2025 DeepSWE agent model. Epoch lists 'DeepSWE v1.1'.

entries.name: FrontierCode
entries.why: Hard coding/agent capability signal included in contemporary capability indices.

verification.note: Launched 2026-06-08; current version is FrontierCode 1.1 (Jul 2026). Splits: Diamond 50, Main 100, Extended 150. Tasks are unreleased and scored on mergeability. It is on Epoch's ECI list.

entries.name: ProofBench
entries.why: Important for verifiable proof/reasoning capability.

verification.note: Vals AI's Lean 4 benchmark, currently v1.1; the paper calls it 'FormalProofBench'. Scored on a private 100-problem split. Not the 2025 natural-language ProofBench (arXiv 2510.13888). Release date from paper.

entries.name: ExploitBench
entries.why: Realistic exploitation/security capability evaluation.

verification.note: Current release is v0.1, covering V8 only: 41 bugs in the paper, 16 flags in 5 tiers. Epoch lists it as 'ExploitBench v0.1'. Otherwise consistent.

entries.name: PostTrainBench v1.1
entries.why: Measures capabilities associated with post-training workflows.

verification.note: Launched Mar 2026; v1.1 came out 2026-07-28. Agents get one H100 for 10 hours to post-train small base LLMs. Epoch lists 'PostTrainBench v1.1'.

entries.name: AgentCompass
entries.why: Extensible OpenCompass-family infrastructure specifically aimed at LLM/VLM agents; active in 2026.

verification.note: List links the open-compass org page, not the repo. Supports 20+ benchmarks, 10+ harnesses; repo commits from 2025-09, tech report 2026-07, EMNLP 2026 Demo.

entries.name: LMMs-Eval
entries.why: Unified text/image/video/audio evaluation with 100+ tasks.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: README advertises 100+ tasks across text, image, video and audio; v0.1 first release 2024-03.

entries.name: VLMEvalKit
entries.why: One-command VLM benchmarking and broad model/dataset support; increasingly integrated into OpenCompass.

verification.note: List links OpenDataArena/VLMEvalKit, an unattributed 0-star copy made 2025-12; canonical is open-compass/VLMEvalKit (220+ LMMs, 80+ benchmarks). It is an OpenCompass project, not newly 'integrated'.

entries.name: OpenVLM Leaderboard
entries.why: Useful common leaderboard around standardized VLM evaluations.

verification.note: Official title 'Open VLM Leaderboard' (HF Space created 2024-01), populated by VLMEvalKit results; a separate OpenVLM video leaderboard also exists. Claims consistent with source.

entries.name: MMMU-Pro
entries.why: Removes many text-only shortcuts and introduces harder visual reasoning conditions.

verification.note: List link is the shared MMMU repo, which hosts MMMU-Pro code (mmmu-pro folder). Claims consistent: filters text-only-answerable questions, augments options, adds vision-only setting.

entries.name: Video-MME
entries.why: Broad video understanding evaluation and increasingly treated as an industry-standard multimodal test.

verification.note: Claims consistent: 900 videos, 2,700 QA; README cites OpenAI GPT-4.1 calling it an 'industry standard measure'. Repo moved from BradyFU (redirects); Video-MME-v2 now exists.

entries.name: MME-RealWorld
entries.why: Stronger emphasis on difficult real-world high-resolution visual scenarios.

verification.note: Claims consistent: 13,366 high-resolution images (avg 2000x1500), 29,429 human-annotated QA, 43 subtasks. Repo moved from yfzhang114 to MME-Benchmarks org (redirects).

entries.name: MMStar
entries.why: Explicitly filters tasks where text alone can solve the problem and studies multimodal leakage.

verification.note: Claims consistent: 1,500 vision-indispensable samples; defines multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage metrics. NeurIPS 2024.

entries.name: OCRBench
entries.why: Important for OCR-centric VLM and document intelligence evaluation.

verification.note: OCRBench (1,000 QA) first appears in arXiv v5, 2024-01; paper v1 (2023-05) predates the name. Successor OCRBench v2 (2024-12, arXiv 2501.00321) adds a private test set.

entries.name: LongBench v2
entries.why: Contexts from 8K to extremely long inputs, emphasizing deeper understanding rather than needle retrieval.

verification.note: List links bys0318/LongBench-v2, the first author's personal fork (3 stars); canonical repo is THUDM/LongBench. Claims consistent: 503 questions, contexts 8k to 2M words.

entries.name: RULER
entries.why: Measures effective rather than advertised context length across configurable long-context tasks.

verification.note: Claims consistent: synthetic, configurable length/complexity; 13 tasks in 4 categories; reports claimed vs effective length. Paper's hsiehjackson/RULER link redirects to NVIDIA/RULER.

entries.name: InfiniteBench
entries.why: Stress test for very-long-context model behavior.

verification.note: Paper titles it '∞Bench'. 12 tasks, 100K+ token average, English/Chinese. Code/data commits from 2023-11; arXiv paper 2024-02 (ACL 2024). Claims consistent.

entries.name: HELM Safety
entries.why: Standardized public safety evaluation across multiple risk categories.

verification.note: List pins release v1.3.0 (2025-04); latest is v1.17.0 (2025-11). 5 benchmarks, 6 risk categories. No paper; introduced by CRFM blog post 2024-11-08.

entries.name: HarmBench
entries.why: Canonical harmful-behavior and jailbreak evaluation suite.
entries.org: Center for AI Safety (with UIUC et al.)

verification.note: Claims consistent: standardized automated red-teaming and robust-refusal framework; initial release compared 18 red-teaming methods against 33 target LLMs and defenses.

entries.name: JailbreakBench
entries.why: Open benchmark for attacks, defenses and jailbreak artifacts with an official leaderboard.
entries.org: UPenn / ETH Zurich / EPFL / Sony AI

verification.note: Claims consistent: JBB-Behaviors (100 harmful + 100 benign), jailbreak artifacts repo, attack and defense leaderboards. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks.

entries.name: StrongREJECT
entries.why: Better than naive refusal scoring for measuring harmful-request compliance.

verification.note: Original repo alexandrasouly/strongreject is deprecated in favour of dsbowen/strong_reject. 313 forbidden prompts plus autograder. Claims consistent.

entries.name: Agent Security Bench
entries.why: Security evaluation specifically for tool-using autonomous agents.

verification.note: Abbreviated ASB; ICLR 2025. Covers 10 agent scenarios with prompt-injection, memory-poisoning and plan-of-thought backdoor attacks plus defenses. Claims consistent.

entries.name: CyberSecEval
entries.why: Security/cyber capability and risk evaluation.

verification.note: Part of Meta's Purple Llama; current version is CyberSecEval 4 (adds AutoPatchBench and CyberSOCEval). Claims consistent.

entries.name: ToolSandbox
entries.why: Tests stateful tool interactions where tool-call sequence and world state matter.

verification.note: Repo moved from apple/ToolSandbox (paper's link, now redirects) to apple-aiml-research. Stateful, conversational, interactive tool-use benchmark; claims consistent.

entries.name: NVIDIA garak
entries.why: Mature vulnerability scanner covering jailbreaks, injection, leakage, hallucination and toxicity.

verification.note: Claims consistent: probes hallucination, data leakage, prompt injection, misinformation, toxicity, jailbreaks. Originally leondz/garak (redirects); first PyPI release 2023-06.

entries.name: Microsoft PyRIT
entries.why: Highly relevant enterprise adversarial-testing framework with reusable attack scenarios.

verification.note: List link is a 2026-07-09 blog post on Scenarios (pre-packaged red-teaming playbooks), matching the claim. Repo moved from Azure/PyRIT (archived placeholder) to microsoft/PyRIT.

entries.name: Inspect Evals Register
entries.why: Important bridge between standardized benchmark definitions and the Inspect execution stack.

verification.note: List links legacy docs/methodology.md, not the Register. Register (beta) replaced /src submissions from 2026-05-08, listing externally hosted evals via YAML. Maintained by Generality Labs.

entries.name: DeepEval
entries.why: Excellent pytest-native unit/regression evaluation; now supports end-to-end, component and trajectory evaluation with 50+ metrics.

verification.note: Claims consistent: docs state 50+ ready-to-use metrics, pytest-style assertions, and end-to-end, component-level and trajectory evaluation.

entries.name: Confident AI
entries.why: Managed collaboration/observability layer around DeepEval; useful when local eval code has to become a team/production workflow.

verification.note: List links deepeval.com (DeepEval homepage, which promotes Confident AI) rather than confident-ai.com. Released = company founding date from site metadata; platform launch date unconfirmed.

entries.name: Ragas
entries.why: Still one of the canonical RAG-specific evaluation toolkits; evolving toward experiment-oriented APIs.

verification.note: List links the evaluate() reference, now deprecated in favour of @experiment, consistent with the experiment-oriented claim. Repo moved from explodinggradients to vibrantlabsai (redirects).

entries.name: Promptfoo
entries.why: Strong CI-native prompt/model/agent regression framework with deterministic assertions and red-team capabilities.

verification.note: OpenAI agreed to acquire Promptfoo (announced 2026-03-09); official README now says 'Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI', still MIT open source. Capability claims consistent.

entries.name: LangSmith
entries.why: Strong offline benchmarking, regression, backtesting, LLM judges and online evaluation integrated with tracing.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: docs cover offline benchmarking, regression, backtesting, pairwise, LLM-as-judge and online evaluation. Announced July 2023 in closed beta; repo is the client SDK.

entries.name: Braintrust
entries.why: Strong experiment-driven production evaluation workflow.

verification.note: Claims consistent; site now brands it an 'observability platform for agents' with evals as a core pillar. Independent (Series B Feb 2026). Repo is the SDK; autoevals is separate.

entries.name: Arize Phoenix
entries.why: Strong traces + evaluation combination, especially RAG/agent debugging.

verification.note: Tracing plus evaluation claims consistent. Caveat: licensed under Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, self-hostable), not an OSI open-source licence. Launched April 2023.

entries.name: Weights & Biases Weave
entries.why: Natural choice for teams already using W&B experiments/artifacts.

verification.currentName: W&B Weave (Weights & Biases, a CoreWeave company)
verification.note: Product name unchanged, but CoreWeave completed its acquisition of Weights & Biases on 2025-05-05. Weave SDK is Apache-2.0; evaluations run on the W&B platform. GA Dec 2024.

entries.name: MLflow GenAI Evaluation
entries.why: Serious 2026 option: datasets, judges, human feedback, traces, production monitoring and `mlflow.genai.evaluate`.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: mlflow.genai.evaluate, LLM-judge scorers, human feedback, tracing and production monitoring. The mlflow.genai evaluation API arrived with MLflow 3.0 (June 2025).

entries.name: Langfuse
entries.why: Particularly good evaluation loop from production traces → datasets → experiments → deployment monitoring.

verification.note: ClickHouse acquired Langfuse (2026-01-16); name unchanged, stays open source and self-hostable, Langfuse Cloud continues. Evaluation claims consistent.

entries.name: TruLens
entries.why: Mature feedback/evaluator model and strong RAG/agent instrumentation.

verification.note: Name unchanged; creator TruEra was acquired by Snowflake in 2024, and Snowflake now maintains TruLens (MIT) under the truera/trulens repo. Feedback-function and RAG/agent claims consistent.

entries.name: Opik
entries.why: Test suites, datasets, quantitative metrics and agent tracing.

verification.note: Claims consistent with source: test suites with LLM-judge assertions, datasets, metrics and tracing. Apache-2.0 with hosted Comet option. Launched 17 Sept 2024.

entries.name: Patronus AI
entries.why: Specialized evaluator API, experiments, production scoring and hallucination/safety evaluation.

verification.note: List link returns HTTP 401 (docs now gated: 'contact support for access'). Company now leads with digital world models and RL environments; eval platform, Lynx, GLIDER and Percival still listed.

entries.name: Giskard
entries.why: Strong behavioral testing, LLM judges, vulnerability scanning and CI/CD.

verification.note: Claims broadly consistent. Open-source library (Apache-2.0, v3) moved to Giskard-AI/giskard-oss; continuous red teaming and team features are in the commercial Giskard Hub.

entries.name: Galileo
entries.why: Production-focused model/application evaluation and monitoring.

verification.note: Cisco announced the Galileo acquisition 2026-04-09 and later completed it. Splunk says 'Galileo – now Splunk Agent Observability'. galileo.ai is still online. Repo is the Python client.

entries.name: HoneyHive
entries.why: Experiment and trace-based LLM application evaluation.

verification.note: Active and independent: no acquisition or shutdown found. GA announced April 2025; SDK 1.6.0 released Sept 2026. Experiments, evaluators and tracing claims consistent.

entries.name: Parea
entries.why: Dataset/evaluator/experiment workflow for model and prompt iteration.

verification.note: Appears defunct: parea.ai and app.parea.ai return HTTP 402 (Vercel deployment disabled) as of 2026-09-25. Last SDK release Feb 2025; only docs remain. No acquisition found.

entries.name: Vellum
entries.why: Good application-level comparison when evals need to sit next to orchestration/workflow tooling.

verification.note: vellum.ai now markets a personal AI assistant, and /enterprise redirects to it. Workflow and Evaluations docs remain on docs.vellum.ai; check it is still sold before listing.

entries.name: Maxim AI
entries.why: Broader production experimentation/evaluation environment.

verification.note: Claims consistent: experimentation, simulation, evals and observability. getmaxim.ai homepage now leads with its Bifrost AI gateway; the eval platform lives at /evals. GA June 2024.

entries.name: Evidently AI
entries.why: Useful where LLM quality evaluation must live beside conventional ML/data monitoring.

verification.note: Claims consistent: an Apache-2.0 library covering LLM evals alongside classic ML/data monitoring, plus commercial Evidently Cloud. No acquisition found.

entries.name: Azure AI Evaluation SDK
entries.why: Strong enterprise evaluator library covering groundedness, relevance, safety, retrieval and agent-specific tool-call/task-adherence evaluation.

verification.note: Evaluator claims consistent, including TaskAdherence, ToolCallAccuracy and IntentResolution; package active (1.18.6, Sept 2026). Its how-to docs now sit under 'Microsoft Foundry (classic)'; AI-assisted evaluators need Azure.

entries.name: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation
entries.why: Managed Google Cloud model/application evaluation.

verification.note: Vertex AI is now Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; Google maps 'Gen AI evaluation service on Vertex AI' to 'Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Evals'. List link is legacy, no longer updated.

entries.name: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations
entries.why: Supports automated, LLM-judge, human and RAG evaluations, including non-Bedrock sources.

verification.note: Claims consistent: automatic, human, LLM-as-judge and RAG evaluations, including models and RAG sources outside Bedrock. Preview at re:Invent 2023; GA April 2024.

entries.name: EvalScope
entries.why: Useful one-stop ModelScope framework spanning LLM/VLM capability eval and inference-performance benchmarking.

verification.note: Claims consistent: LLM/VLM/AIGC evaluation plus performance stress testing, Apache-2.0. First published on PyPI as 'llmuses' (renamed July 2024). No arXiv paper; README cites a 2024 @misc.

entries.name: WeirdML v2
entries.why: Current hard benchmark included in Epoch's capability-index input set.

verification.note: In Epoch's ECI as 'WeirdML (v2)'. Creator has since released v3 (11 agentic tasks) and says v2 (17 tasks, 92.3% SOTA) is near saturation. Only selected task prompts public.

entries.name: Surface Evolver Bench
entries.why: Specialized difficult scientific/computational task signal used in current frontier composite evaluation.

verification.note: Listed in Epoch's ECI. Agentic task: write Surface Evolver .fe liquid-surface simulations, graded against hidden reference metrics. Harness is Apache-2.0; scored tasks are private. Repo commits date from June 2026.

entries.name: Earthborne Rangers / EBR-bench
entries.why: Tests whether systems improve through repeated interaction rather than measuring only static knowledge.

verification.note: Claims consistent: measures score improvement across repeated playthroughs, and is in the ECI. Epoch-run with no public harness; game content not distributed. Launch report published 2026-07-01.

entries.name: Mystery Game Puzzles
entries.why: Useful niche evaluation of inference under deliberately undisclosed game structure; tracked by Epoch.

verification.note: Tracked by Epoch and in the ECI. Epoch describes 100 best-next-move puzzles from a well-known game whose identity is withheld to prevent preparation, not 'hidden-rule' inference. Prompts unpublished.
